III. Read the passage and answer the questions (Questions 32–37 - 1.2 pts)

The Jrai are an ethnic minority group in Viet Nam. They are one of the largest minority groups in the Central Highlands, and many Jrai people live mainly in Gia Lai Province. Their villages are often close to nature, with forests, fields and rivers around them.

The Jrai usually live in stilt houses. They have a rich traditional culture with folk dances, songs, traditional games and musical instruments. They also decorate houses for the dead with wooden statues. These statues show their ideas about life, family and the world around them.

The Jrai economy is connected with farming and nature. Many people earn their living from growing crops, weaving, planting industrial trees and raising buffaloes. In some families, women have a dominant role. They make important decisions and help keep family traditions alive.

Learning about the Jrai helps students understand the diversity of Vietnamese culture. It also teaches young people to respect different customs, houses, costumes and ways of life. In my opinion, this knowledge is useful because it makes students proud of their country’s cultural richness.

MINI REVIEW & KNOWLEDGE SUMMARY

Tổng hợp kiến thức trọng tâm bài học Unit 4 để ghi nhớ sâu.

Từ Vựng Trọng Tâm

  • Ethnic minority groups: Các dân tộc thiểu số
  • Stilt houses: Nhà sàn truyền thống
  • Earn a living from + V-ing: Kiếm sống từ việc làm gì
  • Wooden statues: Tượng gỗ trang trí
  • Diversity: Sự đa dạng phong phú

Cấu Trúc Ngữ Pháp

  • Asking opinion: What do you think about + V-ing?
  • Giving opinion: In my opinion, S + V / I think S + V
  • There is + N (ít) / There are + N (nhiều)
  • Preposition + V-ing: from farming, about living...
